blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, which call is the one intended for measuring elapsed time precisely?

options.text: Instant.now(), since it carries nanosecond digits
options.says: The page says Instant.now() reads the wall clock, which can jump with NTP corrections or manual changes.
The page says currentTimeMillis() also reads the wall clock, which can jump.

options.text: System.nanoTime(), since it is a monotonic clock
options.says: The page names System.nanoTime() as the monotonic clock intended for measuring elapsed time.

questions.stem: Per this page, how do you find the calendar month in which an Instant falls?

options.text: Convert it to a ZonedDateTime in a chosen zone and read the month
options.says: The page says an Instant has no calendar fields such as getMonth() and must be converted to a ZonedDateTime first.

options.text: Call its own month getter, which reports the month as seen in UTC
options.says: The page says an Instant has no getMonth() or other calendar field accessors.

options.text: Divide its epoch seconds by the length of an average calendar month
options.says: The page says a calendar field needs a conversion to ZonedDateTime; epoch seconds alone carry no calendar.

concepts: Instant.now() and currentTimeMillis read a wall clock that can jump, while System.nanoTime is the monotonic clock for measuring elapsed time.
An Instant has no month or day-of-week fields; it must be put in a zone, as a ZonedDateTime, first.
